name: yellide
description: Find what you shot. Indexes your video, audio and photos across every folder and drive, describes what is in them with your own AI, and keeps it searchable when the drive is unplugged.
long_description:
ಎಲ್ಲಿದೆ: Kannada for “where is it?”

Yellide makes the media you have made searchable by WHAT IS IN IT, not only by what the files are called. It indexes wherever your media lives, internal disk, external drives, iCloud, Dropbox, and you never tell it a path. It finds your media itself and ranks the locations by how much is there.

Dates, cameras, lenses, places and durations are read straight out of the files in seconds. Then Claude looks at your pictures and writes down what it sees, and one description covers a whole shoot, so a few minutes of looking can make hundreds of files findable by subject. Ask for the cycling event, not for IMG_4471.MOV.

Everything stays on your machine. It reads only metadata headers plus the first and last megabyte of each file (to identify it), never modifies, moves or renames anything, and sends nothing about you. The one thing it does send is six counts, for a figure on the website, which you can stop by asking. Online-only iCloud and Dropbox files are listed by name and never downloaded. ID cards and medical reports can be marked private: recorded by type only, never by content.

Once a drive is indexed it stays searchable after you unplug it. Yellide will tell you which drive to fetch. Deleting a file removes the bytes, not the knowledge: the entry stays, marked missing.

To start, or after an update: quit Claude with Cmd-Q and reopen it, then in a new chat ask “what media files do I have on this Mac?”. That starts indexing in the background, and everything it finds is searchable by name within seconds. To update, drag the new file on and click Update; it does not update itself. “Run the Yellide diagnostics” shows which version is running.

Ask it: “what media files do I have on this Mac?” · “describe what is in my photos” · “find the cycling event” · “what did I shoot in March 2020?” · “open that one”.

tools.name: describe_archive
tools.description: The photo, video and audio files on this computer and its drives, not past conversations. Call first for any question about them.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search filenames, folders, cameras, dates and tags. Does not yet match image or audio content.

tools.name: get_asset
tools.description: Everything known about one file, and every copy of it.

tools.name: reveal
tools.description: Open it in Finder, or say which drive to fetch.

tools.name: discover
tools.description: Find where the media lives. No path needed.

tools.name: scan
tools.description: Build or update the index in the background. No path needed.

tools.name: export
tools.description: Write the whole index to plain JSON.

tools.name: get_work
tools.description: Shoot representatives that still need a caption.

tools.name: look
tools.description: Show the actual pictures so they can be described.

tools.name: write_annotations
tools.description: Save captions and tags; searchable immediately.

tools.name: caption_next
tools.description: The captioning loop: next undescribed shoots plus their pictures, in one call.

tools.name: diagnostics
tools.description: A shareable health report, counts and capabilities only, no filenames or paths.

tools.name: show_pictures
tools.description: Open a contact sheet of the actual frames, captioned and clickable.

tools.name: import_photo_albums
tools.description: Tag files with the album names you already typed in the macOS Photos app.

tools.name: set_contribution
tools.description: Turn the website counter back on after stopping it.

tools.name: stop_contributing
tools.description: Stop the website counter and delete your row from it.

restrict_to_folders.title: Optional: look only in these folders
restrict_to_folders.description: Leave this empty. Yellide finds your photos and videos by itself, so you never need to choose a folder. Add folders here only if you want Yellide to look in them and nowhere else. Do not drag a media folder into the chat window: Claude will try to read every file into the conversation.

never_write_to_my_drives.title: Never write anything to my drives
never_write_to_my_drives.description: Leave this off if you want Yellide to recognise your drives. Yellide puts one small file, .yellide/volume-id, on each external drive it indexes. The file holds only a random number, nothing about you or your photos. It is how Yellide knows a drive even after you rename it, and how it keeps apart two memory cards with the same name. Turn this on only if nothing at all may be written to your drives. Search still works fully, but a renamed drive looks like a new one, and two cards with the same name get mixed up.
